approval.trigger: Every public connection must be 'submitted for review' before the Authorization URL is even issued, i.e. before your first user can connect. Notion states no criteria, timeline, or rejection handling for this step in the retrievable docs. A separate Marketplace listing review (optional, for discoverability) also has no stated timeline.
approval.wait: Unknown: Notion publishes no timeline for either review

blockers.detail: The Authorization URL field only populates after you submit the public connection for review, and the docs state no criteria, timeline, or resubmission process for this gate. The opacity is itself the risk: you cannot plan around it.
blockers.howToClear: Submit early with complete distribution info; treat the timeline as unknown and have a fallback provider.
blockers.title: Opaque 'submit for review' gate before first OAuth

blockers.detail: At creation you choose installation scope: 'Any workspace' (Marketplace-eligible) or 'Selected workspaces only'. It cannot be changed afterward; the restricted choice permanently forfeits Marketplace eligibility.
blockers.howToClear: Choose 'Any workspace' unless you have a concrete reason to restrict.
blockers.title: Installation scope is immutable

blockers.detail: A fresh token sees nothing until the user explicitly picks pages in the page picker during OAuth (or you duplicate a template / create content post-auth). An agent expecting workspace-wide access gets empty results by default.
blockers.howToClear: Design onboarding around the page picker; request a template if it fits your flow.
blockers.title: Page-picker access model

humanMust: Create the connection in the Developer portal under your Notion account (workspace-owner requirement documented)
Choose installation scope and enter redirect URIs
Supply distribution assets (company info, privacy policy, terms, support email)
name: Notion
nuances: Notion uses capabilities (Content read/update/insert, Comments, User info), not OAuth scopes; changing capabilities after users authorize forces re-authentication, so pick the minimum up front.
The code exchange must run server-side: Notion's /v1/oauth/* endpoints intentionally send no CORS headers.
Tokens are bearer credentials with full granted scope; the docs are explicit about secret-manager storage, never in browser code or version control.
Marketplace listing is explicitly optional: 'you can ship whenever you're ready' and list later, unlike Slack's workspace-count gate.
prerequisites: A Notion account (docs state workspace-owner is required to create a connection)
Distribution info: company name, website, tagline, privacy policy, terms of use, support email

steps.detail: Sign in to Notion, open the Developer portal, create a new public connection. Fill in connection details, redirect URI(s) under OAuth Domain & URIs, and set installation scope to 'Any workspace'.
steps.title: Create the public connection

steps.detail: Submit the connection for review. The Authorization URL field only populates after this step, so no user can OAuth until it clears. Notion states no criteria or timeline; treat the wait as unknown.
steps.title: Submit for review (required)

steps.detail: From the Configuration tab, copy the OAuth Client ID and Client Secret. Never commit them to source control.
steps.title: Copy OAuth credentials

steps.detail: Send the user to api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, owner=user, state. They see your requested capabilities, pick pages in the page picker, and click Allow access (denial returns an error param).
steps.title: Implement the authorize redirect

steps.detail: POST api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token with HTTP Basic auth (base64 client_id:client_secret) and JSON body {grant_type: 'authorization_code', code, redirect_uri}. Note: redirect_uri is required in the body if it was sent as a query param or if you configured more than one URI, otherwise it must be omitted. The code exchange must run on your server (no CORS on Notion's OAuth endpoints). Response: access_token, refresh_token, bot_id, workspace_id.
steps.title: Exchange the code for tokens

steps.detail: (Optional, discoverability only) Start a listing from the Listings dashboard and submit for review; the Notion team reviews every submission and you can resubmit after feedback. No timeline is stated.
steps.title: (Optional) List on the Notion Marketplace

tagline: Straightforward OAuth, but a mandatory review gates your very first user connection, and Notion publishes no criteria or timeline for it. Plan around the unknown.

time.active: ~1-2 hours of portal config + OAuth backend work
time.total: Hours of work, then an unknown review wait before first user connection
time.waiting: Unknown: no timeline published for the required connection review
